profile.summary: DRfold predicts the 3D (tertiary) structure of an RNA from its nucleotide sequence alone, without a multiple sequence alignment. Deep learning models trained on solved RNA structures predict both coarse nucleotide positions and inter-nucleotide geometry; these are combined into an energy function that guides structure assembly. The output is a refined all-atom model in PDB format.
profile.summary_source_locator: Paper: Abstract; Methods: Feature preparation and embedding; README: Example

summary_quotes.text: We present a novel method, DRfold, to predict RNA tertiary structures by simultaneous learning of local frame rotations and geometric restraints from experimentally solved RNA structures, where the learned knowledge is converted into a hybrid energy potential to guide RNA structure assembly.
The only required input of DRfold is the nucleotide sequence
DRfold was trained only on single sequences
' DPR.pdb ': is the final results of DRfold

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: DRfold encodes the sequence as one-hot vectors (A, U, G, C and N for unknown) and adds secondary structure predicted by RNAfold and PETfold as pair features. A stack of 48 transformer blocks, extended from AlphaFold2's Evoformer, updates sequence and pair representations, with 3 recycles. Two kinds of model are trained. End-to-end models use a structure module with invariant point attention to place each nucleotide as a rigid three-bead unit (C4', P and glycosidic N). Geometry models predict inter-nucleotide geometry restraints. Both outputs are combined into a hybrid energy potential that is minimised to assemble a coarse-grained structure. Arena rebuilds full atoms and OpenMM refines the model.

sections.title: Training data
sections.body: The training set holds 3864 unique RNAs from the PDB deposited before 2021. Test structures deposited in or after 2021, and their sequence cluster members, were excluded from training. Training crops were limited to under 200 nucleotides because of GPU memory (a single Nvidia A40 GPU). The training and test sets are available for download from the authors' website.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: The GitHub repository does not include the trained models; they are downloaded separately as DRfold_models.zip from the Zhang group website. A run uses 6 end-to-end models and 3 geometry models; the final model is DPR.pdb. A result should name the repository commit (this page read 9586990c) and the date the model archive was downloaded, since the archive has no version number in the sources read.

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: Ab initio RNA tertiary structure prediction from a single sequence, using deep learning potentials and structure assembly.
facts.source_locator: README: What is DRfold?; Paper: Methods

quotes.text: DRfold (Deep RNA fold) is a program for RNA tertiary structure prediction based on deep learning potentials.
DRfold is a deep machine learning-based approach to ab initio RNA structure prediction.

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: 48 transformer blocks extended from the AlphaFold2 Evoformer (sequence and pair representations of 64 channels), with an IPA structure module for the end-to-end models and geometry heads for the geometry models; energy minimisation, Arena full-atom reconstruction and OpenMM refinement.

quotes.text: There are a total of 48 transformer blocks in DRfold
After the embedding layer, each residue and residue-residue pair will be represented by a 64-D vector.
It consists of three steps of end-to-end frame and geometric potential training, deep-potential-guided 3D structure assembly simulations, and full-atom structure reconstruction and refinement

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: One RNA sequence in a FASTA file. No MSA is needed; secondary structure is predicted internally with RNAfold and PETfold. Modified or unknown nucleotides are encoded as N.

strengths.text: Needs only the sequence: no multiple sequence alignment or database search, which suits RNAs with few homologues.

quotes.text: to facilitate the modeling of hard RNAs without many homologous sequences, DRfold was trained only on single sequences

strengths.text: Training and test sets are separated by deposition date and sequence clustering, and both sets can be downloaded.

quotes.text: a filter based on both sequence identity and time stamp implements a stringent separation between the training and testing datasets of DRfold

strengths.text: The authors report a TM-score more than 73.3% higher than previous approaches on recently released, sequence-nonredundant structures. This is the authors' own claim.

quotes.text: The method significantly outperforms previous approaches by >73.3% in TM-score on a sequence-nonredundant dataset containing recently released structures.

strengths.text: Code is MIT licensed according to the README.

quotes.text: DRfold can be used under The MIT License

limitations.text: Accuracy drops for RNAs longer than 200 nucleotides, because training was limited to shorter crops.

quotes.text: made the current models fall short on large-size RNA modeling as demonstrated in both the benchmark and CASP15 experiments

limitations.text: Non-canonical base pairs are often predicted wrongly.

quotes.text: the success rate of non-canonical base-pairing prediction (INF_nwc) by DRfold was still low

limitations.text: Slow: about 1 hour for a 50-nucleotide RNA, and under 2 hours for the test example.

run_guide.summary: Install DRfold at a pinned commit with its model files and third-party tools, then predict the structure of the bundled test sequence.
prerequisites: A Linux system with Python 3, numpy, scipy, PyTorch and OpenMM; Anaconda is recommended.
PETfold v2.0, the ViennaRNA Package and Arena installed, with their paths set in scripts/Features.py and DRfold.sh as the README describes.
GPU type and memory for inference are not stated in the sources read.
MIT licence, as stated in the README.

steps.title: Download the model files
steps.explanation: The README says to download and unzip the archive, then merge the files in the unzipped DRfold folder into the repository so that models sit under DeepE2EPotential/model and DeepGeoPotential/config*/model. steps.title: Set tool paths
steps.explanation: Sets executable permission on the bundled binaries. Before running, edit scripts/Feature.py ('petfoldbin', 'ViennaRNAbin') and lines 6 and 7 of DRfold.sh (PETFOLDBIN, PYTHON) to match your installation, as the README instructs; the chmod command is added for the permission step.

export PETFOLDBIN="/home/liyangum/projects/RNA/DRfold/bin/PETfold/bin"

steps.title: Run the example
steps.explanation: Runs the full pipeline on the bundled test sequence and writes results to test/DRfold_out.

quotes.text: bash DRfold.sh test/seq.fasta test/DRfold_out

outputs: In test/DRfold_out: DPR.pdb, the final model; DPR_0.pdb to DPR_5.pdb from the 6 end-to-end models; geo.npy with averaged geometry predictions. The README says this takes less than 2 hours.
limitations: These commands were read from the repository and have not been executed by Rewire.
The model merge and path edits are manual steps described in the README, not commands.
The README spells the feature script as Features.py in one place, but the repository file is scripts/Feature.py.

notes: GitHub reports no licence for the repository; the MIT statement is in readme.txt only. The README says 'Features.py' while the script DRfold.sh calls scripts/Feature.py. A separate later repository, leeyang/DRfold2, was seen in a GitHub search; it is a different model and was not reviewed.
